audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL execution mechanics (gas economics, EVM opcodes, precompiles, state transitions, block validation) and CL interactions (RANDAO via beacon chain, validator withdrawal requests, fork activation). Both EL and CL are materially present.

out_of_scope: Beacon chain state transitions beyond EL interface

misclassified_entities.reason: Not an external entity per se — this represents arbitrary input bytes provided via the calling contract's CALL data. The actual external entity is the calling contract (EXT-CALLER). Untrusted data is a data flow property, not a separate entity.

This is an internal smart contract that consumes PREVRANDAO. It is inside the EVM execution environment and not an external entity sending data into the system. It is a potential victim, not a threat source.

EIP authors participate in governance, not in runtime data flows. They do not send data into the EL or CL at execution time. EIP-7773 is a meta-EIP about upgrade coordination, not a protocol-level data flow.

Client development teams configure activation parameters at build time, not at runtime. They are not external entities in the trust model sense of sending untrusted data across a boundary during execution.

L2 rollups deploy RIP precompiles in their own execution environments. From the L1 EL perspective, L2 rollups do not send data into the L1 precompile address resolution process at runtime. EIP-7587 is an address reservation standard, not a runtime data flow.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network (devp2p) — block propagation, transaction gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the P2P network and send blocks or transactions. Blocks may contain invalid difficulty, invalid PoW, malformed headers, or crafted transactions. Covers: EXT-PEER-NODE (EIP-1588, EIP-5133), EXT-NETWORK-PEER (Berlin).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners produce blocks but are untrusted. A miner can produce blocks with manipulated difficulty, timestamps, or transaction ordering. Covers: EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER (EIP-1588), EXT-MINER (Berlin, EIP-5133).

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via public RPC endpoints. Transactions may be malformed, contain malicious calldata, attempt gas manipulation, or exploit access list processing. Covers: EXT-TX-SENDER (Berlin), EXT-BLOB-TX-SUBMITTER (Cancun gas).

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL opcodes to precompile addresses
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any deployed contract can call precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input may be malformed, oversized, or crafted to exploit gas pricing or cryptographic verification. Covers: EXT-CALLER (SHA256, EIP-7002), EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT (point evaluation), EXT-CONTRACT (EIP-7587).

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated, but payload content (RANDAO values, withdrawal requests from CL processing) must still be validated. A compromised CL could inject arbitrary RANDAO values or malformed withdrawal request processing results. Covers: EXT-BEACON-CHAIN (EIP-4399), EXT-BLOB-TRANSACTION (point evaluation — blob commitments originate from CL-validated transactions).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator) via CL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain block proposal — RANDAO reveal
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks and contribute RANDAO reveals. A malicious proposer can bias RANDAO by choosing to skip slots (1 bit of influence per slot). The proposer is not trusted for randomness quality. Covers: EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER (EIP-4399), EXT-MALICIOUS-PROPOSER (EIP-4399).

trusted_external_entities.name: Withdrawal Credential Owner via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC — transaction calling withdrawal predeploy contract (0x00...7002)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any account can call the withdrawal predeploy contract. The EL records msg.sender but does not validate withdrawal credentials — that is deferred to the CL. Malicious callers may spam requests, submit invalid pubkeys, or attempt fee manipulation. Covers: EXT-WITHDRAWAL-CREDENTIAL-OWNER (EIP-7002).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block reception — header validation, PoW verification, difficulty check
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: header fields, PoW (pre-merge), difficulty calculation, ommer validation, transaction root, state root, receipt root. Reject blocks with invalid difficulty (EIP-5133 bomb delay must be correctly applied). Reject blocks failing PoW verification (EIP-1588 fork rules).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P transaction gossip — transaction pool ingestion
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transactions must pass full validation: signature recovery, nonce check, balance sufficiency, gas limit, sender is EOA. Access list transactions (Berlin) require access list format validation.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation — block header with difficulty and PoW
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block difficulty must match expected calculation. Post-fork blocks must use adjusted fake_block_number for bomb delay (EIP-5133). PoW must be valid against the correct ruleset (pre/post ProgPoW for EIP-1588). Timestamp manipulation must be bounded.

Full transaction validation: signature, nonce, balance >= gas*price + value, gas limit within block gas limit. For blob transactions: blob gas pricing validation, max_fee_per_blob_gas >= blob_base_fee. For access list transactions: valid access list format, gas charged for pre-warming.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM CALL to precompile addresses (0x02 SHA256, 0x0A point evaluation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Precompile must validate input format and charge gas before execution. SHA256: charge GAS_SHA256 + GAS_SHA256_WORD * word_count. Point evaluation: verify exactly 192 bytes input, validate versioned hash format, validate KZG commitment/proof as valid G1 points, verify field elements < BLS_MODULUS, charge fixed 50000 gas.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API — block header mixHash field containing RANDAO
boundary_edges.security_assumption: EL must accept RANDAO value from CL via authenticated Engine API but applications must understand RANDAO is biasable (1 bit per proposer). Post-merge blocks should have RANDAO value > 2^64 (heuristic). EL does not validate RANDAO correctness — that is CL's responsibility.

EL processes withdrawal requests dequeued by system call. CL must validate withdrawal credentials match source_address. EL trusts CL for credential validation but must correctly execute the predeploy contract's queue management (max 16 dequeues per block).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon block proposal — RANDAO reveal field
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must verify RANDAO reveal is valid BLS signature. Proposer can bias by 1 bit (skip slot). Applications using PREVRANDAO must implement commit-reveal with multi-epoch delay. CL cannot prevent proposer from choosing to skip.

Predeploy contract must validate: calldata is exactly 56 bytes (or 0 for fee query), msg.value >= current_fee (exponential pricing prevents spam). EL records source_address but does NOT validate withdrawal credentials — CL performs that check. Fee mechanism must correctly implement EIP-1559-style exponential pricing to prevent griefing.

coverage_analysis.notes: 5 entities from source files were reclassified as misclassified (EXT-UNTRUSTED-DATA, EXT-DEPENDENT-CONTRACT, EXT-EIP-AUTHOR, EXT-CLIENT-TEAMS, EXT-L2-ROLLUP). 7 refined entities defined with full boundary edge coverage. All archetypal attack vectors (malicious user via RPC, malicious peer via P2P, malicious validator via CL, malicious external service via Engine API) are represented.
